title: AnomalyMatch finds over 1,300 unusual objects in the Hubble archive
summary: The neural network scanned about 100 million cutouts from the Hubble Legacy Archive in roughly two and a half days: nearly 1,400 anomalies were flagged and over 1,300 confirmed, including more than 800 not previously documented in the literature (mergers, lenses, and jellyfish galaxies). AI only ranks candidates; the two counts are not explained, and no false-positive rate is given.

evidence.tested: The neural network screened about 100 million Hubble Legacy Archive cutouts, and the authors personally inspected the top-ranked sources; more than 1,300 were confirmed as true anomalies, of which more than 800 were not previously documented; no false-positive rate is given.
evidence.unknown: The release gives no false-positive rate, does not state how many candidates were inspected, notes that several dozen objects defied classification, and says expert review is still required.
evidence.ai_role: AnomalyMatch, a neural network, screened the archive and ranked candidate anomalies for expert inspection.
